title: Cisco and Nvidia: Quantum networks will be hybrid or bust
key_facts: Speaking at QDA Forum 2026 in London, Cisco engineer Luca Della Chiesa said the links between quantum systems, or between quantum and classical systems, are a bottleneck that stops quantum parts working together at scale.
He said the winner will be whoever builds the best system, not the best qubits, and that quantum machines will have to fit into existing data centers.
Andy Grant, Nvidia's EMEA director for supercomputing and AI, described plugging quantum processors into existing supercomputers as extra accelerators using Nvidia's NVQLink connection.
Nvidia says its approach, unveiled in July, gives a 2.5-times faster decoding speedup and a three-fold improvement in logical error rates; an AI-based predecoder compresses error information first.
In a Quantinuum, Pfizer and Nvidia collaboration, generative AI was used to design quantum circuits for molecule modelling; Quantinuum reported a 234-times faster generation of training data.
Both companies argued that open tools, formats and shared benchmarks are needed to bring quantum networking into the mainstream.
quote_evidence: “The winner will not be who will build the best qubits, the best entanglement rate. The winner, and this I think Nvidia knows very well, is who builds the best system,” Della Chiesa said, referring to the chip giant.
Grant said Nvidia’s approach, unveiled in July, sees 2.5-times faster decode speedup and three-fold improvement in logical errors rates (LER).
Like Cisco, Nvidia argued only open interoperability would bring quantum networking into the mainstream.
why_it_matters_hint: Two big networking and chip vendors say quantum machines will have to plug into ordinary data centers using open standards.
event_date: QDA Forum 2026, London, around 1-2 Oct 2026 (exact dates not stated; a sister article says the forum ran over two days).
notes: Conference talks by vendors; performance figures are Nvidia's own and its approach was first announced in July. Same forum as C15-08.
